items.text: The another argument from iconographic point of view is rooted in the description of the Sapta Mātṛkās. who are said to be the auspicious manifestations of the goddess (12.13). The idea of seven-mothers was first time conceived iconographically in the Kushan period. These mothers were known as divine female figures with their right hand raised in अभयमुद्रा and holding Kamandlu in left hand, without any distinguishing symbol or vehicle. But as we come to the Gupta period, the distinct Vāhanas and Āyudhās of the different Mātṛkas begin to appear.
